title: File Naming Guide
slide_intent: Make production choices visible in filenames so people can select the right asset without opening every version.
strategic_value: A consistent ordered name can reduce confusion between Burger King logo variants, usage sizes and color spaces.
demonstration: A large BK_Logo_Primary_ST_PMS_C.ai example sits over six labeled columns decoding name, asset type, asset name, asset format, color space and file format.
practical_value: Read or construct a filename by its ordered attributes and underscore separators, checking the usage and color-space codes before choosing a file.

content_islands.name: Naming rationale
content_islands.spec: Place the concise explanation of findability, abbreviations and underscore separation at left.

content_islands.name: Worked filename
content_islands.spec: Set the complete example prominently across the upper right.

content_islands.name: Attribute key
content_islands.spec: Align six columns beneath it, retaining ST/SU/LU usage definitions, CMYK/RGB/Pantone choices and ai/png/jpg formats.

reference_purposes.Intent: The copy says the convention helps users easily find the correct logo file and keeps names concise.
reference_purposes.Application: The worked filename and six-column key show the naming structure and abbreviations.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The source states that attributes follow in order of importance and are separated by underscores.

ingredient.name: Asset filename structure
ingredient.role: Expose the asset’s intended variant and production format before opening it.
ingredient.application: Use the ordered attribute convention and underscore separators illustrated by BK_Logo_Primary_ST_PMS_C.ai. Interpret ST as standard lockup, SU as small usage, LU as large usage and PMS_C/PMS_U as coated/uncoated Pantone.
ingredient.scope: Historical asset-delivery convention; the page describes filenames rather than granting new asset-use permissions.
